title: fault_injection plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `fault_injection` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component FaultInjectionConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

FaultInjectionConfig.description: Plugin: fault_injection — Probabilistic aborts and latency injection for chaos testing. HTTP-family faults run in before_proxy; TCP/UDP/DTLS session admission faults run on stream connect; UDP/DTLS also apply per-datagram faults on on_udp_datagram (client→backend) in isolated session workers without blocking the shared recv loop. Each fault side is decided once per first contact: a session's first client→backend datagram (the plain-UDP opening packet, or the first DTLS application datagram after an admitted handshake) has its abort decided only by stream connect and its delay only by the datagram hook. Optional `match.headers` targets HTTP-family requests and `expires_at` ends the experiment.

status_code.description: Final HTTP status returned when the abort fault triggers. JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 503.0) are accepted as integers.

percentage.description: Abort probability as a percentage. Positive values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up to that first bucket.

grpc_status.description: Optional gRPC status emitted only for native application/grpc requests; plain HTTP, WebSocket, and gRPC-Web rejects omit it. JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 14.0) are accepted as integers.

body.description: HTTP response body returned with the abort. Null is equivalent to omission and yields an empty body. Non-gRPC responses label a body that parses as JSON `application/json` and every other body, including empty, `text/plain`. Native gRPC still normalizes to trailers-only.

duration_ms.description: Delay duration before continuing or aborting, capped at one minute. JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 80.0) are accepted as integers.

percentage.description: Delay probability as a percentage. Positive values below one 64-bit sampler bucket round up to that first bucket.

runtime_overlay_scope.description:
Optional RTDS scope containing at least one non-whitespace
character after Rust `str::trim` Unicode White_Space trimming;
null is equivalent to omission. The published pattern uses the same
White_Space set as Rust (including U+0085, excluding U+FEFF), not
ECMAScript `\S`. The accepted request epoch captures
`ferrum.fault_injection.<scope>.abort_percent` and `.delay_percent`
atomically with this plugin config. Missing or malformed keys fall
back independently to the static percentage.

match.description: Optional blast-radius targeting; null is equivalent to omission. An HTTP-family request is faulted only when every configured header is present on the client-sent request with a field line exactly equal to the configured value; unmatched requests are never faulted and consume no roll. Raw TCP connections and UDP/DTLS datagrams carry no request headers, so an instance with `match` never faults stream or datagram traffic.

headers.description: Header name to exact expected value. Names are valid HTTP header names, matched case-insensitively and unique ignoring case; gateway-asserted names (`x-consumer-*`, the private GeoIP header, path-param headers) are rejected. Values are valid HTTP header values compared byte-for-byte (case-sensitive) against each field line. Values are redacted in non-admin projections.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp (offset required) ending the experiment; null is equivalent to omission. From this wall-clock instant every hook of the instance is a no-op. A timestamp already in the past is accepted and leaves the instance inert, so a stored config that outlives its experiment never blocks a restart or reload.
